narrative:

That comparatively low later-year standing pushed the prediction toward failure more than anything else. The second strongest factor was your first-year class standing: you were in the third decile versus an accepted-student average near the sixth, which also pushed toward failure. The third most influential factor was your LSAT score. At 30 it was below the accepted-student average of 37.18, but in this individual prediction that factor nudged the assessment slightly toward passing rather than failing.

To improve a future application, focus on demonstrating stronger academic performance, especially in upper-year law coursework, and ask admissions for feedback. Consider retaking the LSAT if you can meaningfully raise your score, and reapply once your record shows a clear upward trend. If there were extenuating circumstances affecting your early or later-year grades, address them directly in your application.
